rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After announcing the Resurrection, the passage prompts rational reflection as a reminder and warning.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle haşr u neşrin vukū‘u haber verildikten sonra aklen de onu düşündürmesi lâzım gelen bir tezkir ve ihtar

rows.speaker: Atâ
rows.claim: Atā reports that the verse was revealed concerning Walid b. Mughirah.
rows.anchor: Atâ’dan, bu âyetin Velîd b. Mugīre sebebiyle

rows.speaker: İkrime
rows.claim: Ikrimah reports that the verse was revealed concerning Ubayy b. Khalaf.
rows.anchor: İkrime’den Übey b. Halef sebebiyle nâzil olduğu

rows.speaker: Kelbî ve Mukātil
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil report that the verse was revealed concerning Asad b. Kelede.
rows.anchor: Kelbî ve Mukātil’den de Esed b. Kelede sebebiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the offender struck the Prophet; God did not punish him immediately but revealed this verse.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’e vurmuştu. Allah teâlâ hemen ona ukūbet buyurmayıp bu âyeti inzal eyledi

rows.speaker: birçokları
rows.claim: Many commentators take “the human” here to mean a disbelieving human, in light of the following denial of the Judgment.
rows.anchor: birçokları burada “insan”dan murad kâfir insan demek olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author favors the word’s general scope: all people who rebel through delusion are included, since a specific occasion does not restrict a general ruling.
rows.anchor: sebebin hususiyeti hükmün umumiyetine mâni‘olmayacağı cihetle diğer birçokları da gurur ile isyan eden insanların hepsine şâmil olması lafzın umûmuna daha muvâfık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what made the person arrogant, deceived, and led him into disobedience and unworthy conduct.
rows.anchor: seni ne mağrur etti ne şey aldattı, iğfal etti de isyâna sevketti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this is a warning, invoking the Lord as Generous rather than emphasizing punitive attributes conveys a subtle moral lesson about divine generosity.
rows.anchor: Bu hitab ve sual inzar hitâbı olmak hasebiyle gurûra mâni‘olacak kahr u celâl sıfatlarından biri zikrolunmak zâhir görünürken, “Kerîm” vasfıyla bilhassa kerem-i ilâhînin ihtar olunmasında ince bir nükte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s generosity calls for greater faith, gratitude, obedience, respect, and moral elevation, with avoidance of ingratitude and rebellion.
rows.anchor: iman ve şükran ile tâ‘ati

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating generosity as leave to sin—“God is generous, so do as you wish”—is a false analogy; generosity is joined with wisdom, and generosity used without wisdom would be wastefulness.
rows.anchor: Şeytanların dediği gibi “adam sen de, Allah Kerîm’dir, istediğini yap, dünyada sana ettiği fazl u keremini âhirette de eder” diyerek lâubâlîlik etmek, yanlış bir kıyas ile aldanmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies this warning against being deceived about God with the teaching of Fatir 35:5.
rows.anchor: ihtar edilmiştir ki bu mâna tamamen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author rejects the widespread reading that the question prompts the answer “Your generosity deluded me,” because it conflicts with the surah’s warning tone.
rows.anchor: Bu suâli bazıları “beni keremin mağrur etti yâ Rab!” dedirtmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer who sins despite knowing God’s generosity feels shame and remorse at this address, a response unbelievers cannot feel in the same way.
rows.anchor: kerem-i ilâhîye imanı olduğu hâlde âsî olmuş bir mü’minin bu hitabdan duyacağı hicab ve teessür, kâfirlerin duyamayacağı bir hiss-i teessür

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith calls Suhayb an excellent servant who would not disobey God even if he did not fear Him.
rows.anchor: نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ صُهَيْب لَوْ لَمْ يَخَفِ اللهَ لَمْ يـَعْصِهِ “Suheyb ne güzel kuldur, Allah’tan korkmasa idi bile isyan etmezdi”

rows.speaker: Bazı ârifînin
rows.claim: Some spiritual knowers express the same reverence by saying that even without fear of God they could not disobey.
rows.anchor: Bazı ârifînin “Allah’tan korkmasa idim yine isyan edemezdim”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatir 35:28 states that those servants who truly fear God are the learned; the author links reverential fear to knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: âyeti de bunu nâtık olduğu geçmişti

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Qatadah identifies Satan’s embellishment as what deludes people; the author connects the report to Hadid 57:14.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den mervî olduğu üzere, Şeytan’ın tesvîlidir. وَغَرَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan identifies ignorance as what deludes people.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan mervî olduğu üzere, cehalettir

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil says people are deluded into expecting pardon because punishment was not imposed immediately.
rows.anchor: Mukātil’den rivayet edildiği üzere, evvelemirde ukūbet

rows.speaker: Fuzayl b. İyaz
rows.claim: Asked what he would answer on Judgment Day, Fudayl says he would answer: “Your lowered veils,” meaning God’s concealment of sins.
rows.anchor: Fuzayl b. İyaz Hazretleri’ne “kıyamet günü مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلْكَرِيمِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trusting delayed punishment or divine concealment reduces to ignorance; being taken in by Satan’s embellishment does too.
rows.anchor: bu son ikisi, yani ikābda acele edilmediğinden dolayı affa ve setre güvenmek cehalete râci‘dir. Şeytan’ın tesvîlâtına aldanmak da öyle demektir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: Reports recorded by Abu Hayyan and Alusi say the Prophet recited this verse and answered, “Ignorance.”
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân’ın ve Âlûsî’nin kaydettikleri vechile Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den rivayet olunmuştur ki bu âyeti kıraat etmiş de جهل demiştir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer
rows.claim: Umar likewise answered “ignorance” and recited Ahzab 33:72.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer radıyallahu anh da bunu söyleyip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation as ignorance accords with the restriction in Fatir 35:28: fear of God grows in proportion to one’s knowledge of Him.
rows.anchor: kasrına muvâfakati de âşikârdır. Demek ki haşyet Allah’a dair bilginin derecesiyle mütenâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “created” means bringing into existence initially, as it precedes shaping, balancing, forming, and composing the human being.
rows.anchor: O Rabbin ki seni halketti burada “halk”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Existence, the foundation of every blessing, is the first instance of the Lord’s generosity.
rows.anchor: Ve mâlum ki her nimetin esası olan vücud

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God develops the human through stages to human maturity, fit to receive the spirit, and orders and perfects the body, limbs, and faculties.
rows.anchor: bünyeni, a‘zâlarını, kuvvelerini düzenine koydu, düzgünleştirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God gave the human proportion, balance, and moderation.
rows.anchor: İkisi de bir mânaya olarak denkleştirmek ve mutedil kılmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two readings use a light or doubled dāl, from ʿadl or taʿdīl; both mean balancing and making moderate, completing the account of human formation.
rows.anchor: Burada biri “adl”den dâl’ın feth u tahfîfiyle

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil explains the phrase as symmetry of paired organs and proportion throughout the body, like the balancing of fingertips in Qiyama 75:4; the author says this does not distinctly express human uniqueness.
rows.anchor: Mukātil’den rivayet edildiğine göre göz, kulak, el, ayak gibi çift a‘zâların denkliği

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Atā transmits Ibn Abbas’s view that God straightened the human back and made him upright, unlike crooked-backed beasts; the author finds its human specificity and place after shaping clearer.
rows.anchor: Atâ’nın İbn Abbas’tan rivayet ettiği vecihte ise “belini doğrulttu, kāim mutedil kıldı, eğri belli behâim gibi yapmadı”

rows.speaker: Ebû Ali Fârisî
rows.claim: Al-Farisi explains “made you balanced” as encompassing the best form, human capacity for reason, thought, and power, and the resulting superiority over other creatures and bodies.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüsü, Ebû Ali Fârisî’nin beyânına göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human capacities and excellence described in the preceding interpretation are all forms of divine generosity, in keeping with Hijr 15:29 and Isra 17:70.
rows.anchor: Ve bunların hepsi kerem-i ilâhîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With light dāl, the phrase is also interpreted as turning, bending, or changing direction.
rows.anchor: Bundan başka tahfif ile فَعَدَلَكَ udûl ettirmek, imâle edip çevirmek mânasına dahi tefsir edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is that God repeatedly turned the human from deficiency and an unsuitable form toward perfection and the best form, expressing successive stages of divine selection.
rows.anchor: Birincisi “noksandan kemâle, mülâyim olmayan suretten mülâyim olan surete çevire çevire en güzel surete getirdi” demek olarak yine ıstıfâ merâtibini ifade etmiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, after bringing the human to the best form, God may turn him from perfection to a lower state; this warns those deluded by generosity and supports inference to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: tesviye ile ahsen-i takvîme getirildikten sonra ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَٰهُ أَسْفَلَ سَٰفِلِينَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second “Kalla” recalls the earlier rebuke at 83:7, turning people from cheating and denial toward repentance and good deeds through a reminder of the righteous’ record in Illiyyin.
rows.anchor: Bu “kellâ” tâ yukarıdaki كَلَّآ إِنَّ كِتَٰبَ ٱلْفُجَّارِ’daki “kellâ”ya nâzır olarak tatfif ve tekzibden bir daha zecr ile birr ü hayra sevketmek üzere kıyam gününün diğer bir yüzünü ihtardır

rows.speaker: Ebu’l-feth b. Cinnî
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni derives Illiyyin from ʿuluww, on the fiʿīl pattern, as a plural whose underlying form is illiyyūn.
rows.anchor: Ebu’l-feth b. Cinnî demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Zeccâc
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the word declines like a plural because it has a plural form, like kinnasrin from kinnasr.
rows.anchor: Zeccâc da demiştir ki: “Bu ismin i‘râbı cemi‘

rows.speaker: ehl-i tefsir
rows.claim: One reported interpretation locates Illiyyin in the seventh heaven.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i tefsire gelince: Yedinci semâ denilmiş

rows.speaker: ehl-i tefsir
rows.claim: Another interpretation places Illiyyin at the right foot of the Throne, above the heavens.
rows.anchor: semânın fevkinde Arş’ın kāime-i yümnâsı, yani sağ ayağı denilmiş

rows.speaker: ehl-i tefsir
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies Illiyyin with Sidrat al-Muntaha.
rows.anchor: Sidre-i Müntehâ denilmiş

rows.speaker: Ferrâ
rows.claim: Al-Farra glosses Illiyyin as an endless height, rising from one height to another.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ “yüksekten yükseğe nihâyetsiz” demiş

rows.speaker: Zeccâc
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls Illiyyin the highest of places.
rows.anchor: Zeccâc da “mekânların en yükseği” demiş

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some interpret Illiyyin as exalted ranks endowed by God with majesty and sublimity.
rows.anchor: Bazıları “Allah teâlâ’nın azamet ve ulviyet ile donattığı merâtib-i âliye”

rows.speaker: Diğer bazıları
rows.claim: Others identify it as the location of the angels’ record of deeds.
rows.anchor: diğer bazıları da “melâikenin defter-i a‘mâlinin bulunduğu mevzi‘” demişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author favors Illiyyin as the name of the good-deeds register, opposite Sijjin and witnessed by the near angels, which fits the Quran’s description.
rows.anchor: dîvân-ı şer olan “siccîn”in tam zıddı ve mukarrebînin meşhedi bulunan dîvân-ı hayrın ismi olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may be rendered either “Do you know what Illiyyin is?” or as an exclamation, “How exalted Illiyyin is!”
rows.anchor: Ve bildin mi illiyyûn nedir? Yahut ne illiyyûn!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A marked book may mean a thoroughly and beautifully written record, or one specially marked and sealed by God.
rows.anchor: tam ve güzel yazılmış, yahut Allah tarafından alâmet-i mahsûsa ile tevkī‘buyurulmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the near angels themselves witness the record, see it, and read it, unlike the veiled.
rows.anchor: Mahcûbûn değil, mukarrebûn müşahede eder, onlar görür onlar okurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the near angels attend its writing, preservation, and recitation, and testify to its contents.
rows.anchor: yazılışına, muhafazasına, okunuşuna melâike-i mukarrebûn hazır olur ve mazmûnuna onlar şehadet ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous will be in bliss on the day the wicked are consigned to Hell.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz ebrâr bir na‘îm içindedirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From their couches, the righteous view whichever scenes of Paradise they wish, and also the condition of their enemies in Hell, which the surah explains later.
rows.anchor: Cennetin diledikleri manzaralarına diledikleri gibi nazar edecekler, düşmanları olan ehl-i cehennemin ahvâline de bakacaklardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glow of bliss and the joy and happiness of the righteous are recognizable on their faces to every observer.
rows.anchor: o na‘îmin parıltısını, o nimet ve saadet neş’esinin revnakını yüzlerinde tanırsın yani her gören tanır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahiq is glossed as unmixed, pure wine, also described as the oldest or most pleasant; these are near-synonymous senses.
rows.anchor: “Rahîk” hiç karışığı olmayan hâlis şarab, en eskisi, en hoşu da denilmiş ve hepsinin yakın mânalar olduğu söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: Kāmûs mütercimi
rows.claim: The Kamus translator compares its purity to a rooster’s eye and calls it pure wine, also known as ruhak.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs müterciminin ifadesine göre عَيْنُ الدِّيكِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here rahiq is a white wine of great delight, with no hangover or harmful intoxication, as described in Saffat 37:46–47.
rows.anchor: burada neş’esi ve lezzeti çok, humârı yok

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil indicates this interpretation by glossing the drink as white wine.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Mukātil خَمْرٌ بـَيْضَاء demekle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad 47:15 names four rivers in Paradise, including wine that is pure delight for drinkers; the “likeness” phrasing signals a figurative depiction of complete enjoyment.
rows.anchor: dört nevi cennet ırmaklarından biri de içenlere mahz-ı lezzet olan şarab ırmakları olduğu anlatılırken bunlardan murad neş’e ve lezzetin kemâlini tefhim için temsîlî bir ifade olduğu da baştaki مَثَلُ tâbiriyle anlatılmış idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous drinking from a cup in Insan 76:5 was discussed earlier, and the author directs readers back to that passage.
rows.anchor: Buna dair هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَٰنِ Sûresi’nde

rows.speaker: Hatib tefsiri
rows.claim: Hatib’s commentary treats this rahiq as a special wine beyond the wine rivers mentioned in Muhammad 47:15.
rows.anchor: Hatib tefsirinde der ki: Buradaki rahîk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makhtum means sealed, opened only for those who will drink it; the containers are sealed with musk and are pure and precious.
rows.anchor: ancak içeceklerin nezdinde açılır. Kapları miskten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of “its seal is musk” describes a wine whose delightful finish leaves a musk fragrance, sensed at the end so it does not spoil the taste while drinking.
rows.anchor: hitâmı misk hâtimesi, kesimi misk: içildiği zaman sonu bir misk kokar, içilirken zâika lezzetinin kemâlini ihlâl etmemek için misk kokusu içimin hitâmında duyulmaya başlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because khitam also means a seal, the phrase can mean that the vessel is sealed with musk; both interpretations apply to the drink and its container.
rows.anchor: mühür mânasına geldiğinden “hitâmı misk” demek mührü misk demek olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readings support the interpretation of khitam as a seal.
rows.anchor: Kıraatlerin bazısında خِتَٰمُهُۥ مِسْكٌۭ ve خِتَٰمُهُۥ مِسْكٌۭ okunması da bu mânayı teyid eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musk is an inherent feature of the drink and appears most clearly in its finish; the musk-ending hints at the joy of union, reflected in the righteous’ radiant faces.
rows.anchor: onun levâzımından olup en ziyade hâtimesinde tecellî eder demek olur. Ve hitam ve hâtimesinin böyle misk olması nihâyetinin bir visal neş’esinde karar edeceğini de koklatmış olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation to compete is an inserted parenthesis among the drink’s descriptions, placed at the moment its musk fragrance is noticed to spur immediate striving.
rows.anchor: Bu cümle rahîkin vasıfları arasında bir cümle-i mu‘terizadır. Bundan sonraki vasfını beyandan evvel, tam bu misk kokusunun duyulması lahzasında ona imrendirerek sür‘atle müsabakaya tergīb ve teşvik için araya dercolunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” could refer to bliss or rahiq, but the author finds reference to the final musk finish most fitting in both structure and meaning.
rows.anchor: hitâmına ircâ‘ise hem nazm hem mânaca daha

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing “in that” restricts the competition: people should vie for the hereafter’s musk-ending rahiq, especially its musk finish, rather than worldly wine.
rows.anchor: Bu zarfın takdîmi de kasr içindir. Yani dünya şarablarında lezzetlerinde değil, o gün ebrâra sunulacak olan bu miskiyyü’l-hitâm rahîkte, bâhusus bu misk olan hitamda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munafasa is striving to attain or surpass another’s excellence, an ambition arising from nobility and high aspiration.
rows.anchor: “Münâfese” başkasında görülen bir kemâle imrenip ona yetişmek veya daha ileri gitmek için nefislerin nefâsette yarışması hissidir ki nefsin şerefinden ve uluvv-i himmetinden neş’et eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Competition differs from envy: the envious hate excellence and welcome another’s loss, while a competitor loves excellence and seeks to advance without wishing another to fall.
rows.anchor: Hâsid kemâle düşmandır; mahsûdun zararından, nimetinin zevâlinden memnun olur. Münâfis, yarışçı ise kemâle âşıktır. O karşısındakinin sukūtunu değil, kendisinin daha ileri gitmesini ister

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper field for this competition is good action, as expressed by Saffat 37:61.
rows.anchor: mûcebince hüsn-i amelde müsabaka ile olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasnim is mixed into the rahiq when it is served, making the drink more exquisite than rahiq alone because Tasnim is higher.
rows.anchor: O rahîk içileceği zaman içine tesnîmden de katılır. Bununla mezcolunan rahîk
